title: Carrie Underwood's Ozzy Osbourne cover resurfaces after his final show - NewsBreak
text: An Ozzy Osbourne cover from Carrie Underwood has resurfaced. Ozzy Osbourne, the l egendary rocker from Black Sabbath , ended his live performance career on the evening of Saturday, July 5, and shared a moment with his fans. Fans from all over the world watched Ozzy perform alongside original bandmates Bill Ward, Tony Iommi, and Geezer Butler, possibly for the last time , due to his health struggles. In the wake of the Black Sabbath frontman's last-ever show, fans r esurfaced Carrie's 2023 performance of his 1991 track, "Mama, I'm Coming Home." She performed the song during an appearance on The Howard Stern Show. Carrie was vulnerable and shared how she discovered Ozzy as a teenager. She told the host and audience, "I very much remember being a teenager discovering my own musical tastes, and my mom being very much against me listening to Ozzy." Carrie continued, "I was like, 'I feel like you need to listen to some of these lyrics, 'cause it's not all darkness.' I was like, 'There's a lot of love songs and things that are a lot more melodic and sweet.'" The American Idol host talked about Ozzy's voice that makes him sound a "certain way" and is "very distinguishable." She added, "I don't know what exactly the tricks are because they wouldn't have had all the plug ins and stuff that we have now. He's always sounded the same." DON'T MISS... Ozzy originally wrote "Mama, I'm Coming Home" for his wife, Sharon Osbourne. Carried said that she asks for blessings because she "never wants someone to be like 'Man, I don't like her.'" She went on to say, "I want to be respectful and we had asked permission and Sharon was very sweet about it." Howard Stern shared with Carrie that Ozzy had called him and told him that he "loved" Carrie's performance. Before her iconic 2023 cover, Carrie shared her "Mama, I'm Coming Home" cover and called the song one her "all-time favorite."
